clues: Mountains wrap around this inland city on three sides, in the north of its vast land. Old walls and gates once guarded its palaces and temples.
Hot, damp summers come with the great monsoon winds, but winters are brief, cold, and dry. In spring, sand storms can blow in from a vast desert.
In 1420, this city was named the chief capital of the Ming rulers. Its great palace, built over 14 years, was finished that same year.
From 1406 to 1420, builders raised a vast palace here as the fresh home for the emperors of this land. Hall after hall and yard after yard fill its grounds.
China is ruled from this city today. Lands far away keep 176 embassies here too.
